questions.question: If students on the bus are being disruptive while other students are getting off, what should you do?

options.text: Go to the back of the bus right away to handle the problem while students unload.
Wait until all students are off the bus, then handle the problem.
Have a student close by handle it while you watch the unloading.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until all students are off the bus, then handle the problem.
questions.explanation: The driver must focus completely on loading and unloading students. If behavior problems happen on the bus, wait until all students are safely off and away from the bus before you deal with the problem.

questions.question: During a vehicle inspection, make sure that:

options.text: Emergency exits are hard to open.
Emergency exit warning devices work correctly.
Emergency exits make noise.
Emergency exits cannot be reached from inside the cab.

questions.correctAnswerText: Emergency exit warning devices work correctly.
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection test, check that emergency exit warning devices work. All emergency exits should open smoothly, have no damage, and close firmly from inside.

questions.question: When a school bus picks up students:

options.text: Students must wait at an official bus stop.
The driver can stop to pick up students who are walking to a bus stop.
Parents can decide where the bus stops.

questions.correctAnswerText: Students must wait at an official bus stop.
questions.explanation: School bus drivers can only pick up students at official stops that the school has set.

questions.question: During a vehicle inspection, lug nuts must be all of the following, except:

options.text: Free of cracks.
Free of damage.
Loose.
Free of rust.

questions.correctAnswerText: Loose.
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection test, all lug nuts must be present, free of cracks and damage, and tight. Look for rust marks or shiny threads that show looseness. Check all bolt holes for cracks and damage.

questions.question: During the on-road test, you will be graded on checking traffic. You should not:

options.text: Look for pedestrians on the road.
Check traffic regularly.
Skip checking your mirrors at intersections.
Check your mirrors regularly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Skip checking your mirrors at intersections.
questions.explanation: During the on-road test, check traffic and use your mirrors often, especially at intersections. Look for pedestrians wherever they might be.

questions.question: After students get off at school, the driver should:

options.text: Not worry about where the students go.
Leave after students enter the building.
Walk through the bus to check for sleeping students.

questions.correctAnswerText: Walk through the bus to check for sleeping students.
questions.explanation: After students get off at school, the driver should walk through the bus to look for sleeping students, hidden students, and any items left behind. Students should exit in an orderly way with the driver watching.

questions.question: When should the bus start moving after students board?

options.text: As soon as students finish getting through the door.
When students are near their seats but still standing.
When all students are seated and facing forward.
As soon as students cross the standee line.

questions.correctAnswerText: When all students are seated and facing forward.
questions.explanation: After students board, wait until everyone is seated and facing forward before the bus moves.

questions.question: During the vehicle inspection test, when asked about oil, you must be able to do all of the following, except:

options.text: Show where the dipstick is.
Show that the oil level is safe.
Show that the oil level is above the refill mark.
Show that the oil level is below the refill mark.

questions.correctAnswerText: Show that the oil level is below the refill mark.
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection test, you must show where the dipstick is, confirm the oil level is safe, and show that the oil level is above the refill mark.

questions.question: If you exit your vehicle incorrectly during the basic vehicle control skills test, you will:

options.text: Fail only that exercise.
Get to try that exercise again.
Fail the entire basic vehicle control skills test.
Lose one point.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fail the entire basic vehicle control skills test.
questions.explanation: When you exit the vehicle during the basic vehicle control skills test, always face the vehicle and keep three points of contact. For a bus, hold the handrail. Exiting incorrectly may cause you to fail the entire basic control skills test.

questions.question: During a vehicle inspection, check that the landing gear is:

options.text: Pulled in.
Completely raised.
More worn on one side than the other.
Bright and visible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Completely raised.
questions.explanation: When inspecting the landing gear, make sure no parts are missing and it is fully raised. The crank handle should be secure and the support frame should have no damage.

questions.question: If a driver cannot find a student after the student exits the bus, what should the driver do?

options.text: Lock the bus and search for the student.
Assume the student left safely.
Go to the back of the bus to check if the student got back on.
Ask another student if they saw the missing student.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lock the bus and search for the student.
questions.explanation: If the driver cannot find a student outside the bus, lock the bus and check around and under the bus for the missing student.

questions.question: What is a passive railroad crossing?

options.text: A crossing with a control device.
A crossing with no control devices.
A crossing you should avoid.

questions.correctAnswerText: A crossing with no control devices.
questions.explanation: A passive railroad crossing has no traffic control devices. The driver must decide whether it is safe to cross.

questions.question: Which backing maneuver is NOT part of the basic control skills test?

options.text: Straight line backing
Offset back/right
Offset back/left
Blind offset

questions.correctAnswerText: Blind offset
questions.explanation: The basic control skills test includes straight line backing, offset back/right, offset back/left, driver side parallel parking, conventional parallel parking, and alley docking. Blind offset is not included.

questions.question: During the driving test, what will the examiner score you on?

options.text: How well you speak.
How fast you reach your destination.
Your driving behavior.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your driving behavior.
questions.explanation: The examiner will score you on your driving maneuvers and general driving behavior. You must drive safely, obey all traffic signs and laws, and avoid accidents or moving violations.

questions.question: What should the overhead inside mirror show?

options.text: The area outside the driver's side of the bus.
All students on the bus.
Students in the first four rows only.
The front of the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: All students on the bus.
questions.explanation: Adjust the overhead mirror to show all students, including those sitting right behind the driver.

questions.question: During the on-road driving skills test, you will be tested on gear usage. Which should you avoid?

options.text: Grinding or clashing gears.
Picking a gear that does not rev the engine too much.
Shifting while going through an intersection.
Shifting while turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shifting while turning.
questions.explanation: Choose a gear that does not rev or strain the engine. Avoid grinding gears and do not shift while turning or going through intersections.

questions.question: During the straight line backing exercise, how many times can you exit the vehicle to check its position?

options.text: One time
Two times
Three times
Four times

questions.correctAnswerText: One time
questions.explanation: You may exit your vehicle only once during the straight line backing exercise to check the vehicle's position.

questions.question: When driving through a curve during the skills test, what should you do?

options.text: Leave your lane if needed to complete the curve.
Slow down after entering the curve.
Do not look for other vehicles while turning.
Slow down before entering the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before entering the curve.
questions.explanation: Slow down enough before the curve so you do not need to brake or shift while turning. Stay in your lane and keep checking for traffic.

questions.question: During the stop/start maneuver in the skills test, what should you do?

options.text: Cut off other vehicles to get onto the shoulder.
Do not use turn signals.
Brake hard to stop as quickly as possible.
Slow down gradually.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gradually.
questions.explanation: Check traffic, use your turn signal, and slow down smoothly with even braking. Shift gears as needed and come to a complete stop without coasting.

questions.question: If a student drops something near a stopped bus, what should they do?

options.text: Quickly pick it up.
Leave it behind.
Ask the driver to pick it up.
Have another student pick it up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ask the driver to pick it up.
questions.explanation: Students should not pick up dropped items because they could disappear from the driver's view. Instead, students should get out of the danger zone, get the driver's attention, and ask the driver to retrieve the item.
